exposure: elective caesarean section at 36, 37, 38, and 39 weeks of pregnancy
cohort: 200 newborns born in 2015 and hospitalised from birth in the Department of Neonatology, Pomeranian Medical University in Szczecin
finding: Newborns born via elective caesarean section at 36 and 37 weeks had significantly lower birthweight, lower Apgar scores, lower frequency of breastfeeding, higher rates of hypothermia, observation room and incubator use, respiratory failure, and longer hospital stays compared to those born at 38 and 39 weeks.
